metadata.title: On Weak Chromatic Polynomials of Mixed Graphs

nodes.name: Mixed Graph
nodes.statement: A mixed graph G = (V, E, A) consists of a set of vertices V, a set of undirected edges E (called edges), and a set of directed edges A (called arcs).

nodes.name: k-Coloring of a Mixed Graph
nodes.statement: A k-coloring of a mixed graph G is a mapping c: V -> [k], where [k] := {1, 2, ..., k}.

nodes.name: Weak Proper k-Coloring
nodes.statement: A weak proper k-coloring of G is a k-coloring such that c(u) != c(v) if uv is an edge, and c(u) <= c(v) if uv is an arc directed from u to v.

nodes.name: Strong Proper k-Coloring
nodes.statement: A strong proper k-coloring of G is a k-coloring such that c(u) != c(v) if uv is an edge, and c(u) < c(v) if uv is an arc directed from u to v.

nodes.name: Weak Chromatic Polynomial
nodes.statement: The weak chromatic polynomial chi_G(k) counts the number of weak proper k-colorings of a mixed graph G.

nodes.name: Strong Chromatic Polynomial
nodes.statement: The strong chromatic polynomial hat{chi}_G(k) counts the number of strong proper k-colorings of a mixed graph G.

nodes.name: Orientation of a Mixed Graph
nodes.statement: An orientation of a mixed graph G is obtained by orienting each undirected edge (assigning a head and tail), while arcs cannot be re-oriented.

nodes.name: Acyclic Orientation and Acyclic Mixed Graph
nodes.statement: An orientation of a mixed graph is acyclic if it contains no directed cycles. A mixed graph is acyclic if all of its possible orientations are acyclic.

nodes.name: Compatible Coloring and Orientation
nodes.statement: A coloring c and an orientation of G are compatible if for every u -> v in the orientation, c(u) <= c(v).

nodes.name: Intercompatible Coloring and Orientation
nodes.statement: A coloring c and an orientation of G are intercompatible if for every u -> v in the orientation, c(u) <= c(v) when uv is an edge of G, and c(u) < c(v) when uv is an arc of G.

nodes.name: Strong Chromatic Polynomial Reciprocity (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: For any mixed graph G=(V,E,A) and positive integer k, (-1)^{|V|} hat{chi}_G(-k) equals the number of k-colorings of G, each counted with multiplicity equal to the number of compatible acyclic orientations of G.
assumptions: G = (V, E, A) is a mixed graph
conclusions: (-1)^{|V|} hat{chi}_G(-k) equals the number of k-colorings of G, each counted with multiplicity equal to the number of compatible acyclic orientations of G

nodes.name: Weak Chromatic Polynomial Reciprocity (Theorem 2, Main Result)
nodes.statement: For any acyclic mixed graph G=(V,E,A) and positive integer k, (-1)^{|V|} chi_G(-k) equals the number of k-colorings of G, each counted with multiplicity equal to the number of intercompatible acyclic orientations of G.
assumptions: G = (V, E, A) is an acyclic mixed graph
conclusions: (-1)^{|V|} chi_G(-k) equals the number of k-colorings of G, each counted with multiplicity equal to the number of intercompatible acyclic orientations of G

nodes.name: Partially Ordered Set (Poset)
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: A partially ordered set (poset) is a set P with a relation that is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive.

nodes.name: omega-Labeling
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: An omega-labeling of a poset P with n elements is a bijection omega: P -> [n].

nodes.name: Order Polynomial
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: The order polynomial Omega_{P,omega}(k) counts the number of maps (x_1,...,x_n) in [k]^n such that x_u <= x_v if u preceq v and omega(u) < omega(v), and x_u < x_v if u preceq v and omega(u) > omega(v).

nodes.name: Complementary Labeling
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: The complementary labeling to omega is the labeling bar{omega} defined by bar{omega}(v) := n+1 - omega(v), which swaps the strict and non-strict inequality conditions in the order polynomial.

nodes.name: Stanley's Order Polynomial Reciprocity (Theorem 3)
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Omega_{P,omega}(-k) = (-1)^{|P|} Omega_{P,bar{omega}}(k). The order polynomial evaluated at -k equals, up to sign, the order polynomial with complementary labeling evaluated at k.
assumptions: P is a poset with an omega-labeling

nodes.name: Weak Chromatic Polynomial as Counting Function
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: chi_G(k) = #{(x_1,...,x_n) in [k]^n : x_u <= x_v if uv is an arc, x_u != x_v if uv is an edge}.

nodes.name: phi_{G_i}(k)
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: For an acyclic mixed graph G with orientations G_1,...,G_m, phi_{G_i}(k) is the number of weak proper k-colorings of G_i that are also weak proper k-colorings of G.

nodes.name: Decomposition of Weak Chromatic Polynomial (Lemma 4)
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: If G is an acyclic mixed graph, then chi_G(k) = sum_{i=1}^{m} phi_{G_i}(k), where G_1,...,G_m are the acyclic orientations of G.
assumptions: G is an acyclic mixed graph
G_1, ..., G_m are all acyclic orientations of G

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4 (phi sum)
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Each weak proper k-coloring of G is a weak proper k-coloring of some G_i. Conversely, no coloring can be weak proper for two distinct orientations G_i and G_j (since they differ on some edge orientation, forcing contradictory inequalities). If E(G) is empty, G is its own unique orientation.

nodes.name: omega-Labeling Correspondence (Lemma 5)
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: For each orientation G_i of an acyclic mixed graph G, there exists an omega_i-labeling of the corresponding poset P_i such that phi_{G_i}(k) = Omega_{P_i,omega_i}(k). Moreover, Omega_{P_i,bar{omega}_i}(k) counts the number of k-colorings intercompatible with G_i.
assumptions: G is an acyclic mixed graph
G_i is an acyclic orientation of G
P_i is the poset corresponding to G_i
conclusions: There exists an omega_i-labeling of P_i such that phi_{G_i}(k) = Omega_{P_i,omega_i}(k)
Omega_{P_i,bar{omega}_i}(k) equals the number of k-colorings intercompatible with G_i

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5 (labeling correspondence)
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Constructs omega_i by reversing edges (not arcs) to get R_i, then recursively labeling source vertices. This ensures omega_i(u) < omega_i(v) implies uv is an arc, and omega_i(u) > omega_i(v) implies uv is an edge, matching the order polynomial conditions. The complementary labeling swaps strict/non-strict inequalities, yielding intercompatible colorings.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 (Main Result)
nodes.section: 2 Posets, Order Polynomials, and the Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.proof_strategy: combination of decomposition lemmas and Stanley's reciprocity
nodes.statement: Applies Lemma 4 to decompose chi_G(-k) as a sum over orientations, Lemma 5 to convert each phi_{G_i}(-k) to Omega_{P_i,omega_i}(-k), Stanley's reciprocity (Theorem 3) to obtain (-1)^{|P_i|} Omega_{P_i,bar{omega}_i}(k), and Lemma 5 again to interpret each summand as counting intercompatible colorings.

nodes.name: Deletion and Contraction of Edges and Arcs
nodes.statement: G-e (resp. G-a) is the mixed graph with edge e (resp. arc a) deleted. G/e (resp. G/a) is the mixed graph with edge e (resp. arc a) contracted (deleted and incident vertices identified, removing parallel edges/arcs). G_a is G with arc a reversed.

nodes.name: Deletion-Contraction for Edges (Proposition 6)
nodes.statement: If G is a mixed graph and e is an edge of G, then chi_G(k) = chi_{G-e}(k) - chi_{G/e}(k).
assumptions: e is an edge in E(G)

nodes.name: Arc Reversal G_a
nodes.statement: G_a is the mixed graph G with arc a = uv reversed, i.e., G_a = (V, E, A - {uv} union {vu}).

nodes.name: Deletion-Contraction for Arcs (Proposition 7)
nodes.statement: If G is a mixed graph and a is an arc of G, then chi_G(k) + chi_{G_a}(k) = chi_{G-a}(k) + chi_{G/a}(k).
assumptions: a is an arc in A(G)

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7 (arc deletion-contraction)
nodes.statement: Lets C and C_a be the sets of weak proper k-colorings of G and G_a respectively. Shows chi_G(k) + chi_{G_a}(k) = |C union C_a| + |C intersect C_a|, where |C union C_a| = chi_{G-a}(k) and |C intersect C_a| = chi_{G/a}(k).

nodes.name: Edge Deletion-Contraction Formula
nodes.statement: chi_G(k) = chi_{G-e}(k) - chi_{G/e}(k), the recursive deletion-contraction formula for edges in mixed graphs.

nodes.name: Arc Deletion-Contraction Formula
nodes.statement: chi_G(k) = chi_{G-a}(k) + chi_{G/a}(k) - chi_{G_a}(k), the deletion-contraction formula for arcs in mixed graphs.

nodes.name: Strongly Connected Directed Graph
nodes.statement: A directed graph G = (V, emptyset, A) is strongly connected if for any pair of vertices u, v there exists a directed path from u to v.

nodes.name: Chromatic Polynomial of Strongly Connected Graph (Proposition 8)
nodes.statement: If G is a strongly connected directed graph, then chi_G(k) = k.
assumptions: G is a strongly connected directed graph (no undirected edges)

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 8 (strongly connected)
nodes.statement: For any vertex u, directed paths to and from any other vertex v force c(v) <= c(u) <= c(v), so all vertices must have the same color. There are k choices for this common color.

nodes.name: Strongly Connected Subgraph Contraction (Proposition 9)
nodes.statement: If G is a mixed graph and S is a strongly connected directed subgraph of G, then chi_G(k) = chi_{G/S}(k).
assumptions: S is a strongly connected directed subgraph of G

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 9 (subgraph contraction)
nodes.statement: Vertices of S must all receive the same color in any weak proper k-coloring (by strong connectivity). Assigning this color to the contracted vertex gives a bijection between weak proper k-colorings of G and G/S.
